pages.x: After defeat by Japan and the Boxer disaster, the Qing court tried reforms: it ended the old exams, built a modern army and promised a parliament. But many Chinese, angry at foreign bullying and at rule by the Manchus, wanted the dynasty gone, and secret revolutionary societies spread among students and soldiers.

Sun Yat-sen, a doctor trained in Hong Kong, spent years abroad raising money from Chinese overseas for a revolution, and was even kidnapped by the Chinese embassy in London in 1896. In 1905 he founded the Revolutionary Alliance. Its risings failed one after another.

On 9 October 1911 a bomb went off by accident in a revolutionaries' workshop in Hankou. Police found lists of members, and soldiers in nearby Wuchang, fearing arrest, rose the next night. They took the city, and within weeks most of China's provinces had broken with the Qing. Sun read about it in a newspaper in Denver, Colorado.

Sun hurried home, and on 1 January 1912, in Nanjing, he was sworn in as provisional president of the Republic of China. But the court's strongest general, Yuan Shikai, held the best army in the north. Sun offered Yuan the presidency if he would make the emperor step down.

The emperor, Puyi, was six years old. On 12 February 1912 the empress dowager signed away the throne in his name, ending more than 2,000 years of rule by emperors. Puyi was allowed to stay in the Forbidden City, and lived on to be a puppet emperor for Japan and, in the end, a gardener in Communist Beijing.

Yuan Shikai became president, but soon crushed the new parliament and ruled as a dictator. In 1915 he declared himself emperor. The provinces rebelled, and he gave up the throne after 83 days and died a few months later. China fell into the hands of rival warlords.

The revolution ended China's empire and made it one of Asia's first republics, though not a steady one: decades of warlords, civil war and Japanese invasion followed. Sun Yat-sen is honoured as the father of modern China in both the People's Republic and Taiwan, and 10 October is still Taiwan's national day.
